data.summary: Coil whine is a high-pitched noise emitted by graphics cards (GPUs) and power regulation modules (VRMs) due to vibrations in inductor coils when power runs through them. This phenomenon is common in electrical devices, particularly noticeable during high frame rate scenarios in gaming. The article explains that while some believe running a GPU under stress can reduce coil whine, there is no scientific evidence to support this. Instead, solutions include dampening the noise or moving the case away from the user. EKWB suggests using thermal pads with their water blocks to mitigate the issue.
keyPoints: Coil whine occurs due to vibrations in inductor coils in GPUs and VRMs.
High frame rates during gaming can exacerbate coil whine noise.
Moving the case away or using sound insulation can help reduce noise.
EKWB includes thermal pads with their EK Vector series water blocks to dampen coil whine.
data.improvedTitle: Everything You Need to Know About Coil Whine
